name: Colchicine
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Colchicine clearance falls in kidney impairment and drops by about 75% in end-stage kidney disease on dialysis; it is not removed by hemodialysis. The US label lowers starting doses below creatinine clearance (CrCl) 30 mL/min and in dialysis, and limits repeat flare courses.
kidney_function_basis: Label uses creatinine clearance (CrCl, mL/min; Cockcroft–Gault).

bands.recommendation: Usual dosing; at CrCl 50 to 80 no adjustment but monitor for adverse effects (label).
Gout prophylaxis and flare treatment: no adjustment, monitor closely (label: CrCl 30 to 50). Familial Mediterranean fever (FMF): dose reduction may be needed.
Gout prophylaxis: start 0.3 mg/day, increase with close monitoring. Flare treatment: no dose change, but repeat a course no more than once every 2 weeks. FMF: start 0.3 mg/day (label).
As for CrCl <30 (label 'severe' impairment): prophylaxis 0.3 mg/day start; flare courses no more than every 2 weeks.

hd: Gout prophylaxis: start 0.3 mg twice a week with close monitoring. Flare treatment: single 0.6 mg dose; do not repeat more than once every 2 weeks. FMF: start 0.3 mg/day. Not removed by hemodialysis (label).
pd: Label 'dialysis' wording does not specify modality; same starting doses with close monitoring. Specialist input.
crrt: No data in label. Insufficient data: specialist input.
monitoring: Myotoxicity, neuromyopathy, blood counts, GI toxicity. Avoid flare treatment in kidney impairment if already on prophylaxis. Check CYP3A4/P-glycoprotein inhibitor interactions (label).

pediatric.approved_ages: FMF: 4 years and older. Gout: not established; not recommended in children (label).
pediatric.usual_dose: FMF (label gives age-based fixed doses, not mg/kg): 4 to 6 years 0.3 to 1.8 mg/day; 6 to 12 years 0.9 to 1.8 mg/day; over 12 years 1.2 to 2.4 mg/day, once or in 2 divided doses.

renal.recommendation: No pediatric kidney-dosing data in the US label; specialist (pediatric nephrology) input.

pediatric.egfr_equation: Bedside Schwartz: eGFR (mL/min/1.73 m2) = 0.413 x height (cm) / serum creatinine (mg/dL)
